findings.where: Screen 11 (Precharge): text and the caption after the contactor closes
findings.what: The screen says that after five time constants (0.5 s) only about 2 V of the gap is left and the contactor's blip is about 2 A, but that is true only of the drawn steady-DC feed: fed through the bridge from 230 V AC, the circuit on screen, the link is only about 84% full at 0.5 s with about 50 V left (computed by stepping the ideal-diode circuit), and the lesson's own explain and practice say filling takes several times longer, so add one sentence saying the picture feeds it from steady DC and a bridge-fed link takes several times longer, and qualify or drop the 2 A blip and the caption 'Only a small blip of current flows'.

'When is the capacitor about full?' is asked of a bridge circuit, yet the accepted 0.5 s holds only from steady DC (through the diodes 99.3% takes about 3.6 s, computed), so the right answer contradicts the explain's 'several times longer'; ask 'By the charging curve, when is it about full?' or 'Fed from steady DC, ...'.

The brief promised lesson 3's battery point, that ripple drives a ripple current that heats a battery (VRLA guide, notes 4.5), and it is missing, though it is the use that matters most for a main battery on charge; add it as one or two sentences in the explain and one practice line.

The explain carries five footnotes, and [^1] (what a smoothing capacitor does) and [^3] (the DC link as the store between rectifier and inverter) sit on descriptions rather than a rule or value he would look up, so drop those two markers and keep the 100 Hz, 1.35 and switch-on short-circuit ones.

'A 2 A load on 1000 µF falls 2 V every millisecond' skips the working, even though leaving µF unconverted is one of the lesson's own common mistakes; swap 'Here i is the load current and C the capacitance.' for '2 ÷ 0.001 = 2000 V a second, which is 2 V a millisecond.', which also removes the jump from lowercase i to capital I and keeps the word count.

findings.where: Screen 3 text against the Peak supply current readout
findings.what: The text says each gulp runs at 'several times the load current' while the trace and readout show 35 A for a 2 A load, 17 times, because the drawn supply has no resistance; say once that the drawn gulp is taller and narrower than a real one.

Each screen's text is 88 to 89 words, and the live caption under the picture adds 24 to 25 more, so about 113 words show at once; trim one sentence from each, for example screen 7's 'So a smoothed bus sits between the two, near the peak at light load.'

findings.where: Screen 7 (Light load, heavy load): first sentence
findings.what: The screen opens with an instruction, 'Drag the load and watch the bus average fall.', rather than the point; open with 'Load pulls the bus down from the peak.' and put the drag after it.
The key lists 'DC bus' before Check while the bus is hidden, so the key names a line that is not drawn; show or fade in that key entry with the bus.
The right-answer feedback 'Still there.' does not read as a sentence; use the default 'That's it.' or 'Right: five time constants.'

findings.where: Screens 4, 8, 10 and 13: readouts on a right Check
findings.what: On a right Check the readout tiles appear at once above the answer buttons, so at 360 px Check and Continue jump down under his finger; fade the tiles in or place them below the feedback line.
The header-tank pump has no non-return valve, so between surges the tank would drain back through the pump; say 'through a non-return valve', which also ties it to lesson 1's one-way valve.

The bold takeaway runs to 30 words with a chained 'so' clause; split it into two sentences: 'A capacitor across a rectifier fills near each peak and feeds the load between them. The bus holds near the peak, with a ripple of about I ÷ (f × C).'
